sentences.text: The only known fossil of Lavocatavis is a single femur described from the Glib Zegdou Formation in 2011.
The single known femur of Lavocatavis is nearly as large as that of Patagornis.
The genus name Lavocatavis means "Lavocat's bird" and honors René Lavocat, who first reported the geological layer containing the fossil.
Because the Atlantic Ocean separated South America from Africa during the Eocene, researchers suggest Lavocatavis ancestors likely arrived in Africa via rafting on floating islands or island hopping.
Lavocatavis has been tentatively classified as a member of the family Phorusrhacidae, but this placement is considered highly questionable due to fragmentary remains.
Lavocatavis lived during the Eocene epoch in Algeria.
Lavocatavis lived between 56 and 41.03 million years ago during the Ypresian to Lutetian stages.
It is debated whether Lavocatavis ancestors retained some flight ability, which would have allowed them to travel between islands more easily than flightless birds.
